title: OpenPLC CANopen configuration, schema_version 2 (several networks, slave networks, gateway)
description: The CANopen bridge's JSON config with a list of networks (docs/config.md#several-networks): master networks, one CANopen master per CAN interface, and slave networks, where OpenPLC is one CANopen device under another master (docs/slave.md), with an optional gateway between them (docs/gateway.md). A master network's adapter, master and nodes are the version 1 definitions, referenced from canworks.v1.schema.json, except that a PDO entry may leave out iec_location: the bridge allows that only for an entry a gateway route uses. Unknown fields are allowed: the bridge and the deploy tool ignore them with a warning. Checks this schema cannot express (unique names, interfaces and serial devices, IEC locations across networks, slave bindings and gateway routes against the EDS files) are listed in docs/config.md, docs/slave.md and docs/gateway.md.

schema_version.description: Config format version: 2 for a file with a networks list.

diagnostics.description: The diagnostics channel for all networks: one port, one token. In version 1 this is master.diagnostics.

networks.description: The networks: CANopen master networks (one master per CAN interface), CANopen slave networks and J1939 networks ("protocol": "j1939", docs/j1939.md).

cia309.description: The CiA 309-3 ASCII gateway for all networks (docs/cia309-gateway.md). In version 1 this is master.cia309.

not.description: Version 1 keys belong inside a network in version 2.

then.description: A network may list no nodes (scan only) only when the diagnostics channel is configured.

codesys.description: Makes this a CODESYS config, built into a CODESYS project with CODESYS's own CANopen Manager instead of run by canworks-bridge (docs/codesys.md). PDO entries need no iec_location then: CODESYS assigns the I/O addresses and each entry's channel is named by its 'name' or the generated name. canworks-deploy's --codesys-* options override these settings.

project.description: The CODESYS project file the bus is built into (--codesys-import).

device.description: The device in the project that gets the bus. Default: the device of the project's active application, else its only device.

create.description: Creates the project when it does not exist, with this PLC device from CODESYS's device repository: TYPE:ID:VERSION.

variables.description: Name the I/O channels after the entries (default true).

network_codesys.description: A CANopen master network's CODESYS settings (CODESYS configs only).

net_id.description: The CODESYS network number of the network's CANbus. Default: the interface's trailing number, else 0.

interface.description: The device's CAN interface object that gets the network's bus, such as CAN or CAN2. Default: found by name.

bridge.description: The Modbus bridge: canworks-bridge runs the config and serves its values as Modbus TCP registers (docs/modbus-bridge.md); the configurator's `connections` list who uses the registers. Locations are byte addresses then: %IWn covers input bytes n and n+1, word and larger locations start at an even byte, and no two locations share a byte (bits of one byte with different bit numbers excepted). Input byte n is input register n/2, %IXn.b discrete input n*8+b; outputs map to holding registers and coils the same way.

listen.description: address:port to serve Modbus TCP on, a numeric address: 0.0.0.0:502, [::]:502, 192.168.1.10:1502.

unit_id.description: Unit identifier answered (default 1; 0 and 255 are always answered).

word_order.description: Order of the registers of a 32- or 64-bit value (default high_first).

max_clients_per_address.description: Connections served at once from one address (default 4).

writers.description: Required. Addresses or prefixes allowed to write; [] lets nobody write, ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"] every address.

readers.description: Addresses or prefixes allowed to connect (default: every client).

watchdog_ms.description: Outputs off when no write came from a writer for this long (default 1000; 0: no watchdog).

on_client_loss.description: Outputs off: stop (default, no RPDOs or transmit messages), zero (send 0 once, then stop), hold (keep sending) or preop (stop, and every node of every CANopen master network to pre-operational; NMT start when outputs come back).

live_lists.description: 16-byte live lists of CANopen master networks: bit n set while node n is operational.

sdo_bridge_location.description: The SDO bridge registers: a 14-byte request block in the outputs and a 14-byte response block in the inputs.

sdo_bridge_write.description: Allow SDO writes through the SDO bridge registers (default false).

mailboxes.description: Mailboxes for the PLC function blocks (docs/plc-library.md#bridge-blocks): request mailboxes for long SDO, CAN and J1939 operations, a receive mailbox for frames, J1939 messages and EMCY, network info and cyclic CAN jobs. Each area is one block of bytes from input_location and output_location; Pack for Modbus sets both.

requests.description: Request mailboxes, 0-4 (default 1). Blocks share them in turn.

cyclic_jobs.description: Cyclic CAN frames the bridge sends, 0-16 (default 4).

network_info.description: A network info block for each of the first 8 networks (default true).

input_location.description: Where the input area starts, an even input byte.

output_location.description: Where the output area starts, an even output byte.

plc_link.description: The PLC link for any Modbus client that runs the generated canworks_in and canworks_out (docs/plcopen.md): input bytes 0-3 hold the map hash, the status block is at %IB4, output bytes 0-5 hold the PLC link header (running, map hash), and outputs apply only while the header says running with this map's hash.

connections.description: The programs and tools that use the registers (docs/modbus-bridge.md#connections), written by the configurator: each has kind (openplc, trust, plc, nodered or hmi), a unique name, address, writes, the kind's own fields and map_hash, the map hash of its last download. canworks-bridge doesn't read them; the PC check does.

address.description: The client's IP address (127.0.0.1 for openplc).

writes.description: Whether the client writes outputs; bridge.writers follows the connections that do.

map_hash.description: Map hash of the last download, such as 0x1234abcd.

poll_ms.description: openplc: poll period of OpenPLC's Modbus master (default 10).

remote_device.description: openplc: the editor's remote device file name, devices/remote/<name>.json (default canworks).

iec_base.description: openplc: first %IW and %QW index of the remote device's points (default: the lowest free run from 100).

format.description: trust and plc: plcopen or st (st for plc only); hmi: csv, json or st.

library.description: trust and plc with plcopen: include the canworks ST library (default true).

bridge_host.description: trust, plc and nodered: the bridge's address as the client reaches it.

period_ms.description: nodered: poll period of the flow (default 100).

name.description: The network's name in logs, diagnostics, exports and variable names. Default: the adapter's interface name.

protocol.description: "canopen" (default), "j1939" (docs/j1939.md) or "none" (docs/raw-can.md). A J1939 network has 'adapter' and 'j1939', and none of 'role', 'master', 'nodes' and 'slave'. A plain CAN network ("none") has 'adapter' and optionally 'raw', and nothing else.

role.description: "master" (default): OpenPLC is the network's NMT master, with 'master' and 'nodes'. "slave": OpenPLC is one CANopen device under another master, with 'slave' instead (docs/slave.md).

then.description: A plain CAN network has an adapter and its raw messages, and none of the CANopen or J1939 keys.

else.description: Only a plain CAN network is listen-only.

then.description: A J1939 network has an adapter and a j1939 object, none of the CANopen keys, and runs on a real or vcan interface, not on the simulated bus.
A slave network has an adapter and a slave object, and no master or nodes.

else.description: A master network has an adapter, a master and nodes, and no slave object.

raw.description: Raw CAN messages of the network (docs/raw-can.md): frames received into %I and sent from %Q, on any network. The bridge and the deploy tool check the fields themselves, with their own messages; unknown fields are ignored with a warning.

dbc.description: The DBC file the messages came from, relative to the config file (for the tools; the bridge does not read it).

program_override_protocol.description: The program's CAN_SEND and CAN_SEND_CYCLIC may use identifiers the network's protocol uses.

raw_id.description: The CAN identifier: 0..0x7FF, or 0..0x1FFFFFFF with extended.

signal_mux.description: Multiplexing (docs/raw-can.md): the signal is in a frame only when switch `on` has one of `values` (and `on` itself is in the frame). `on` may be left out when the message has one switch.

on.description: The name of a switch (multiplexer: true) of the same message.

values.description: Switch values: whole numbers or [low, high] ranges.

signal_pages.description: How a send message with switches goes out: "program" (default) the page the program's switch outputs select; "all" every page each period; "rotate" the next page each period. With "all" and "rotate" the bridge sets the switches, which then have no iec_location.

start_bit.description: As in a DBC file; for big byte order the most significant bit.

iec_location.description: The raw value's PLC location: %IX/%QX for 1 bit, else the smallest of byte, word, double word or long word that holds it.

valid_location.description: Received signals: a bit input that is TRUE while frames carrying the signal arrive (within the entry's timeout_ms).

multiplexer.description: A switch: its value says which other signals (those with mux on it) the frame carries. Unsigned, at most 32 bits.

mask.description: Identifier bits that must match (default: all).

dlc.description: Only frames with this DLC (default: any that holds the signals).

timeout_ms.description: status_location goes FALSE after this long without the message (0: never).

id_location.description: %ID: the last frame's identifier (with a mask).

data_location.description: %IL: the last frame's 8 data bytes, byte 0 lowest.

dlc.description: Default: the smallest that holds the signals.

fill.description: The value of bytes no signal covers.

override_protocol.description: Send on an identifier the network's protocol uses.

trigger_location.description: %QX: a rising edge sends the message.

j1939.description: A J1939 network (docs/j1939.md): the PLC's ECU identity, the PGNs it receives into %I, the PGNs it sends from %Q and the requests it sends. Signals reach the PLC as raw integers; scale, offset and unit are for the tools and the generated declarations.

dbc.description: The DBC file the messages came from, relative to the config file (for the tools; the bridge does not read it).

requests.description: Requests (PGN 59904) the PLC sends periodically; answers are received like any rx PGN.

address_range.description: [low, high]: the addresses the ECU may move to when it loses its address to a lower NAME (needs arbitrary_address_capable).

state_location.description: Byte input for the claim state: 0 claiming, 1 claimed, 2 cannot claim, 3 no bus.

address_location.description: Byte input for the current source address (254 while none is held).

j1939_name.description: The ECU's 64-bit NAME, field by field. Missing fields are 0 (false).

arbitrary_address_capable.description: The ECU may move to another address in address_range when it loses its address.

j1939_pgn.description: Parameter group number 0..0x3FFFF. A PDU1 PGN (PDU format below 0xF0) has its low byte 0; the destination is given separately.

start_bit.description: The start bit as in a DBC file (big byte order: the most significant bit).

iec_location.description: %I for a received signal, %Q for a sent one, sized to hold the length (X 1 bit, B 8, W 16, D 32, L 64).

valid_location.description: Received signals: a bit input that is FALSE while the signal arrives as not available or error, and for a signal with mux until frames carrying it arrive.

multiplexer.description: A switch: its value says which other signals (those with mux on it) the frame carries. Unsigned, at most 32 bits.

source.description: Take the PGN only from this source address.

source_name.description: Take the PGN only from the ECU with this NAME (64 bits, decimal or 0x hex).

source_name_mask.description: The NAME bits to compare (default: all).

timeout_ms.description: 0 (default): no supervision. Otherwise status_location goes FALSE when no message arrived for this long.

length.description: Message length in bytes; default: the smallest length of at least 8 that holds every signal.

period_ms.description: 0 (default): send on change and on request only.

min_gap_ms.description: Least time between two sends on change (default 0).

j1939_diagnostics.description: Diagnostic messages (J1939-73, docs/j1939.md#diagnostic-messages): ECUs whose DM1 (active trouble codes and lamps) the program sees, and the network's own trouble codes, sent as DM1 every second.

rx.description: ECUs whose DM1 reaches the program's inputs.

dtcs.description: The network's own trouble codes, each switched on by one output bit.

lamps_location.description: Byte output ORed into the lamp byte of the network's DM1 (MIL bits 7-6, red stop 5-4, amber warning 3-2, protect 1-0; 01 on).

clear_location.description: Byte input counting the clears (DM3, DM11) the network carried out, wrapping at 255.

accept_clear.description: false: DM3 and DM11 requests to the network's address are answered with NACK. Default true.

dm13.description: Honour DM13 stop and start broadcast commands. Default true.

source_name.description: Take the DM1 only from the ECU with this NAME (64 bits, decimal or 0x hex).

source_name_mask.description: The NAME bits to compare (default: all).

timeout_ms.description: status_location goes FALSE when no DM1 arrived for this long; 0: no supervision. Default 3000.

status_location.description: Bit input: TRUE while the ECU's DM1 arrives.

lamps_location.description: Byte input: byte 1 of the DM1 (lamp states).

flash_location.description: Byte input: byte 2 of the DM1 (lamp flash).

count_location.description: Byte input: the number of active codes (at most 255).

dtcs_location.description: The first of `dtcs` consecutive double word inputs that get the codes, each SPN + FMI*2^19 + OC*2^24 + CM*2^31.

spn.description: Suspect parameter number (19 bits); 520192..524287 are proprietary.

active_location.description: Bit output: the code is active while TRUE.

lamps.description: Lamps the code lights while active.

field_node.description: A node of a master network: the version 1 node, except that a PDO entry may leave out iec_location (the bridge allows that only for an entry a gateway route uses, or of a TPDO that feeds a PDO link).

slave.description: OpenPLC as one CANopen device on a slave network (docs/slave.md). Everything except the node ID and the PLC bindings comes from the EDS.

node_id.description: The own node ID, 1-127, or null to start without one and wait for an LSS master to assign it.

eds.description: The slave's EDS file, relative to the config file: written by hand, or by canworks-deploy slave-eds.

eds_lint.description: Which dcfgen EDS lint findings stop the load, as master.eds_lint does for nodes. Default: communication.

objects.description: Objects of the slave's dictionary bound to PLC locations. The direction comes from the EDS AccessType: rww and rw objects (the master writes them) need an %I location, ro and rwr objects (the master reads them) a %Q location; const and wo objects cannot be bound.

inputs_on_loss.description: What bound inputs do while the node is not OPERATIONAL or communication is lost: "hold" (default) keeps the last values, "zero" sets them to 0.

state_location.description: An input byte (%IB...) with the own NMT state: 0 not started, 4 stopped, 5 operational, 127 pre-operational.

comm_ok_location.description: An input bit (%IX...): TRUE while OPERATIONAL with no heartbeat consumer or life guarding error.

sync_count_location.description: An input word (%IW...) counting the SYNCs received, wrapping at 65535.

emcy_code_location.description: An output word (%QW...): a change to a non-zero code sends one EMCY with it, a change to 0 the error reset.

error_register_location.description: An output byte (%QB...): the error register sent with the program's EMCY and kept in 0x1001.

name.description: The variable's name in the declarations, after the network name. Default: the object's ParameterName in the EDS.

gateway.description: OpenPLC as a gateway (docs/gateway.md): a slave on the upper network and the master of the other networks, with routes the bridge copies between them without the PLC program.

upper.description: The name of the slave network, whose master is the upper master.

status.description: Field node states in the slave's dictionary: for the k-th master network (k = 0-3) an ARRAY of UNSIGNED8 at index + k (sub-index n: NMT state of node n) and an operational bit field at index + 0x10 + k (sub-indices 1-4: UNSIGNED32, nodes 0-31, 32-63, 64-95, 96-127).

emcy_forward.description: Send each field node's EMCY on the upper network as the gateway's own, with the field network index and node ID in the manufacturer bytes. Default: false.

on_upper_loss.description: What routed values down do when the upper master is lost: "hold" (default) keeps them, "zero" sends 0, "stop_nodes" stops the field nodes that receive routes until the upper master starts the gateway again.

sdo_bridge.description: The SDO bridge record, through which the upper master reads objects of field nodes. Default: false.

sdo_bridge_index.description: The SDO bridge record's index. Default 0x5F00.

sdo_bridge_write.description: Also allow writes to field nodes through the SDO bridge. Default: false.

route.description: One slave object of the upper network and one PDO entry of a field node. The direction comes from the slave object's AccessType: ro and rwr objects are written from a field node's TPDO entry (up), rww and rw objects feed a field node's RPDO entry (down). Both ends have the same data type.

name.description: The route's name: the name the EDS generator gives the slave object.
